SEO AND STRUCTURED DATA Use get-seo/list-seo before set-seo, set-seo-defaults or set-schema. Follow the current target schema: record, term, post-type defaults and archive SEO are not interchangeable. Yoast-dependent operations require Yoast active. get-seo shows whether Yoast is active; when Yoast is missing, ask the site admin to install and activate it. Preserve SEO properties the user did not ask to change. Inspect inherited/default values before overriding. Custom schema is validated structured data; never treat JSON-LD fields as arbitrary JavaScript insertion. Use real content/field values and appropriate schema types, not fabricated ratings or claims.
SEO often is not visible in a screenshot. Verify title, meta tags, canonical/robots/social output and structured data in the response/page source; a saved setting does not prove frontend output. Avoid duplicate/conflicting graph entities. Check the effect on representative records when changing post-type defaults or schemas. Rendering still belongs to the installed SEO plugin and theme. Archive SEO settings are data; the archive layout stays with the theme and templates.
WHICH TOOL FOR WHICH SCOPE One record or one term: set-seo {contentId} / {termId}. A post type's archive: set-seo {archive}. The pattern every record of a type or term of a taxonomy follows: set-seo-defaults {postType} / {taxonomy}. Site-wide values (separator, website name, organisation, social profiles, share image): set-seo-defaults {site:true}.
YOAST VARIABLES IN TITLE AND DESCRIPTION TEMPLATES An unknown variable is removed from the output without an error, so use only these: %%title%% %%excerpt%% %%excerpt_only%% %%date%% %%modified%% %%id%% %%name%% (author) %%parent_title%% %%focuskw%% %%sitename%% %%sitedesc%% %%sep%% %%page%% %%pagenumber%% %%pagetotal%% %%currentyear%% %%currentdate%% %%category%% %%primary_category%% %%tag%% %%pt_single%% %%pt_plural%% On a term: %%term_title%% %%term_description%% %%category_description%% %%tag_description%% %%term_hierarchy%%. Fields: %%fab_<name>%% (a Fabrement field as a reader sees it), %%cf_<meta key>%% (another plugin's meta), %%ct_<taxonomy>%% (a record's terms of that taxonomy). %%sitename%% is the WordPress site title (update-site-settings), not the Yoast website name. In set-schema the tokens are different: {{title}} {{url}} {{site_url}} {{excerpt}} {{featured_image}} {{date_published}} {{date_modified}} {{field:<name>}} {{option:<page>.<field>}} {{meta:<key>}} {{term:<taxonomy>}}; {{excerpt}} there is Yoast's description for the page.
